subject: Board liaison: decision criteria, risks, and procurement timeline
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Lowell <andrew@helixbio.com>, Sara Gomez <sara.gomez@helixbio.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Board liaison: decision criteria, risks, and procurement timeline

Hi Andrew & Sara,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate you walking us through the board's priorities and the technical review cadence. Below is a concise recap for the board liaison packet and the procurement team. I put suggested owners and dates so we can align on next steps quickly.

Key business outcomes you emphasized:
- Reduce model-inference cost per transaction by ~35% while keeping 1.5s p50 latency for batch/real-time mix.
- Improve end-user response consistency (fewer hallucinations in clinical triage) to reduce clinician verification time by ~22%.
- Maintain data residency within your US region and support audit logs for 12 months.

Primary pain points (as discussed):
- Current inference infra has unpredictable tail latency under production traffic spikes.
- Security/compliance gap: existing vendor cannot provide KMS/HSM integration and fine-grained audit logs.
- Procurement needs: single-vendor SOW with a 90-day pilot before a full POC/contract.

Decision criteria the board will use (please confirm):
1) Measured latency and throughput on representative workload (test harness agreed)
2) Clear cost modeling (per-token + ops) to project 12-month TCO
3) Security/compliance evidence (SOC2-type report, KMS integration doc, sample audit event format)
4) Pilot success metrics and go/no-go gate defined in writing

Proposed procurement timeline (draft):
- Week 0 (by 2027-05-28): Delivery of executive summary + TCO model (owner: Irene) [attachment: redwood-exec-summary-helix-20270522.pdf]
- Week 1 (by 2027-06-03): Pilot scope & statement of work (owner: Marissa) [attachment: pilot-scope-proposal-helix.xlsx]
- Week 2-6 (starting 2027-06-07): 30-day pilot execution (owner: Helix + Redwood eng leads)
- Week 7 (by 2027-07-12): Pilot readout to board & procurement decision

Escalation / risk items to flag for the board:
- If SOC2 evidence is required before pilot start, procurement will need to adjust timing (may push pilot start 2–3 weeks).
- Customer data residency requirements will need a Private deployment option; we propose a hybrid approach if network constraints arise.

Immediate asks for Helix: 
- Can you confirm the board's decision gate (who signs the formal go/no-go)?
- Can procurement share required contract templates or security addenda we should expect to see (procurement@helixbio.com)?
- Please send the representative test dataset profile (size, token distribution) or allow us to use a synthetic harness.

I'll circulate the one-page exec summary and the pilot scope in a follow-up (attached). If the timeline above looks off, flag a different target date.

Thanks,

Irene Choi
Head of Solutions - Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Irene — thanks for the clear recap. That aligns well with what the execs asked for. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

- The board decision gate will be the VP of Product (Elena Park) + CFO signoff. They want the pilot readout and cost model in hand.
- Procurement: we'll push the standard SOW but expect a security addendum request. If you can provide KMS integration docs and a sample audit log schema, that will speed review.
- Time: pilot start target is still OK but procurement will triage the security docs first — if SOC2 evidence is required upfront, it may delay start by ~2 weeks.

I'll ask Sara to pull the representative test dataset profile and drop in the drive link.

Thanks Andrew — and hi Sara. Adding the pilot success metrics I promised (so procurement and the board have a concrete gate):

Pilot success metrics (proposed, pass/fail gates):
- Latency: p50 < 1.5s and p95 < 3.0s on the representative test harness (pass if both met for 7 consecutive days).
- Cost: projected monthly inference spend reduction >= 30% compared to baseline (pass if TCO model shows <= 70% baseline within 12 months).
- Quality: automated eval set shows decrease in hallucination rate by at least 20% (human review sample to validate).
- Security: KMS integration verified in staging; audit events emitted and accessible for 12 months.

Operational asks for Helix:
- Provide the dataset profile or a redacted representative sample to model token distribution (drop to the drive link in the next email).
- Point person for procurement (name & contact) so we can exchange SOW & security addenda drafts.

I've uploaded the pilot scope draft to the shared drive and linked the doc in the thread (see related_links). Happy to walk through the scope with your eng lead next week.

—Marissa
